top_violation_types.title: Report Number of Employees (26 TAC §746.303(b))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: A review of the Employees Who Left Employment in 2021 data from February 23, 2022, revealed that the center had not reported the number of employees who left employment in 2021 by February 22, 2022, as required.

top_violation_types.title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: During the investigation and video, it was found that the caregiver did not demonstrate a high level of judgment or self-control.

top_violation_types.title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The ground is splitting open and causing a tripping hazard at the entrance to the playground.       Photos taken

top_violation_types.title: Director Annual Training 30 Hours Required (26 TAC §746.1311(a))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The Director has not completed 30 annual training hours.

top_violation_types.title: Safety - Bodies of Water Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3701(8))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: There is mopping bucket containing water in the prek age room and accessible to children.     Note: This was corrected at inspection when provider removed bucket.

top_violation_types.title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The operation did not have a current fire inspection.

top_violation_types.title: Prohibited Punishments - No Harsh, Cruel or Unusual (26 TAC §746.2805)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Two caregivers were observed administering prohibited punishment. One caregiver was observed pulling a child by the arm from underneath a table and another caregiver was observed grabbing a child by the arm and holding onto the child to keep the child from moving out of a chair. The same caregiver was observed grabbing on a child and pulling on the child's arms.

top_violation_types.title: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization (26 TAC §746.305(a)(2))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: During the investigation, it was determined that the staff was aware of a child receiving medical attention after sustaining an injury while in care, but did not report to Child Care Licensing within two days of becoming notified.
